Teen Mental Health — Modelos de Ensamblado para Regresión

Variable objetivo: stress_level (1–10) | Dataset: datosestresyansiedad.xlsx

Zulema luque

13 de Mayo de 2026

1 Introducción

Este reporte presenta un análisis comparativo de modelos de ensamblado para regresión supervisada, con el objetivo de predecir el nivel de estrés (stress_level, escala 1–10) en adolescentes a partir de variables socioemocionales y de uso de redes sociales.

Se implementan los siguientes modelos:

Modelo Descripción
rpart Árbol de decisión podado por CP óptimo
Bagging Random Forest con mtry = p (todos los predictores)
Random Forest RF con mtry óptimo seleccionado por error OOB
GBM Gradient Boosting con n.trees seleccionado por CV
XGBoost XGBoost con early stopping
XGBoost Tuned XGBoost con búsqueda de hiperparámetros (tidymodels)

La evaluación final usa intervalos de confianza bootstrap (95%) en el conjunto de test, y se complementa con nested CV para una estimación insesgada del error de generalización.

4 Partición estratificada del dataset

La partición se realiza de forma estratificada por cuartiles de stress_level para evitar que algún subconjunto (train/test) concentre valores extremos de la variable respuesta.

set.seed(SEED)
split_obj  <- initial_split(datos, prop = 0.8, strata = stress_level)
data_train <- training(split_obj)
data_test  <- testing(split_obj)

cat(sprintf("Train: %d observaciones | Test: %d observaciones\n",
            nrow(data_train), nrow(data_test)))
## Train: 959 observaciones | Test: 241 observaciones
# Matrices para XGBoost (one-hot encoding automático)
X_train <- model.matrix(stress_level ~ . - 1, data = data_train)
y_train <- data_train$stress_level
X_test  <- model.matrix(stress_level ~ . - 1, data = data_test)
y_test  <- data_test$stress_level
dtrain  <- xgb.DMatrix(data = X_train, label = y_train)
dtest   <- xgb.DMatrix(data = X_test,  label = y_test)

4.1 Verificación de la estratificación

bind_rows(
  data_train %>% select(stress_level) %>% mutate(Conjunto = "Train"),
  data_test  %>% select(stress_level) %>% mutate(Conjunto = "Test")
) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = stress_level, fill = Conjunto)) +

       x = "stress_level", y = "Frecuencia") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 12) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom",
        plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"))

Comparación de distribución de stress_level en train y test

5 Función de métricas con IC bootstrap

Las métricas puntuales sobre un único test set son estimaciones ruidosas. Se calculan RMSE, MAE y R² con sus respectivos intervalos de confianza al 95% por bootstrap (B = 1000 réplicas).

boot_metrics <- function(y, yhat, B = 1000, alpha = 0.05) {
  n <- length(y)
  reps <- replicate(B, {
    idx <- sample.int(n, n, replace = TRUE)
    c(rmse = Metrics::rmse(y[idx], yhat[idx]),
      mae  = Metrics::mae (y[idx], yhat[idx]),
      r2   = 1 - sum((y[idx] - yhat[idx])^2) /
                 sum((y[idx] - mean(y[idx]))^2))
  })
  data.frame(
    metric = c("RMSE", "MAE", "R2"),
    est    = c(Metrics::rmse(y, yhat),
               Metrics::mae (y, yhat),
               1 - sum((y - yhat)^2) / sum((y - mean(y))^2)),
    lower  = apply(reps, 1, quantile, probs = alpha / 2),
    upper  = apply(reps, 1, quantile, probs = 1 - alpha / 2)
  )
}

6 Modelos baseline

6.1 rpart — Árbol de decisión podado

Se ajusta con validación cruzada interna (10 folds) para seleccionar el CP óptimo por menor error de validación cruzada.

set.seed(SEED)
arbol <- rpart(stress_level ~ ., data = data_train, method = "anova",
               control = rpart.control(cp = 0.001, xval = 10))
cp_opt <- arbol$cptable[which.min(arbol$cptable[, "xerror"]), "CP"]
modelo_rpart <- prune(arbol, cp = cp_opt)
rpart.plot(modelo_rpart, main = sprintf("rpart podado (cp = %.4f)", cp_opt),
           type = 4, extra = 101, cex = 0.7)

Árbol de decisión podado con CP óptimo 

pred_rpart <- predict(modelo_rpart, newdata = data_test)
cat(sprintf("RMSE rpart en test: %.4f\n", Metrics::rmse(y_test, pred_rpart)))
## RMSE rpart en test: 2.8696

6.1.1 Curva de poda (CP table)

cp_df <- as.data.frame(arbol$cptable)
ggplot(cp_df, aes(x = CP, y = xerror)) +
  geom_line(color = "steelblue", linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(size = 2, color = "steelblue") +
  geom_point(data = cp_df[which.min(cp_df$xerror), ],
             aes(x = CP, y = xerror), color = "red", size = 4, shape = 18) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = min(cp_df$xerror) + cp_df$xstd[which.min(cp_df$xerror)],
             linetype = "dashed", color = "orange") +
  scale_x_log10() +
  labs(title = "Curva de poda — Error CV vs. CP",
       subtitle = "Punto rojo = CP óptimo | Línea naranja = regla 1-SE",
       x = "CP (escala log)", y = "Error de validación cruzada (xerror)") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 12)

Error de validación cruzada vs. CP (complejidad del árbol)

6.2 Bagging

Random Forest con todos los predictores (mtry = p) — equivalente a Bagging.

set.seed(SEED)
modelo_bag <- randomForest(stress_level ~ ., data = data_train,
                           mtry = ncol(data_train) - 1,
                           ntree = 500, importance = TRUE)
pred_bag <- predict(modelo_bag, newdata = data_test)
cat(sprintf("RMSE Bagging en test: %.4f\n", Metrics::rmse(y_test, pred_bag)))
## RMSE Bagging en test: 2.9340

6.3 Random Forest con mtry óptimo (OOB)

mtry_grid  <- 2:(ncol(data_train) - 1)
oob_errors <- sapply(mtry_grid, function(m) {
  set.seed(SEED)
  rf <- randomForest(stress_level ~ ., data = data_train, mtry = m, ntree = 500)
  tail(rf$mse, 1)
})
mtry_opt <- mtry_grid[which.min(oob_errors)]
cat("mtry óptimo por OOB:", mtry_opt, "\n")
## mtry óptimo por OOB: 2
# Gráfico
data.frame(mtry = mtry_grid, OOB_MSE = oob_errors) %>%
  ggplot(aes(mtry, OOB_MSE)) +
  geom_line(color = "steelblue", linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_point(size = 2.5, color = "steelblue") +
  geom_point(data = data.frame(mtry = mtry_opt,
                               OOB_MSE = oob_errors[which.min(oob_errors)]),
             color = "red", size = 5, shape = 18) +
  labs(title = "Selección de mtry por error OOB",
       subtitle = paste("mtry óptimo =", mtry_opt),
       x = "mtry", y = "OOB MSE") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 12)

Error OOB en función de mtry 

set.seed(SEED)
modelo_rf <- randomForest(stress_level ~ ., data = data_train,
                          mtry = mtry_opt, ntree = 500,
                          nodesize = 3, importance = TRUE)
pred_rf <- predict(modelo_rf, newdata = data_test)
cat(sprintf("RMSE Random Forest en test: %.4f\n", Metrics::rmse(y_test, pred_rf)))
## RMSE Random Forest en test: 2.9332

6.3.1 Convergencia del error OOB por número de árboles

data.frame(ntree = seq_along(modelo_rf$mse), OOB_MSE = modelo_rf$mse) %>%
  ggplot(aes(ntree, OOB_MSE)) +
  geom_line(color = "forestgreen", linewidth = 0.8) +
  labs(title = "Convergencia OOB — Random Forest",
       x = "Número de árboles", y = "OOB MSE") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 12)

Error OOB del Random Forest en función del número de árboles

6.4 GBM con CV interna

set.seed(SEED)
modelo_gbm <- gbm(stress_level ~ ., data = data_train,
                  distribution = "gaussian",
                  n.trees = 5000, interaction.depth = 5,
                  shrinkage = 0.01, n.minobsinnode = 10,
                  bag.fraction = 0.5, cv.folds = 5)
best_iter_gbm <- gbm.perf(modelo_gbm, method = "cv", plot.it = FALSE)
cat("GBM mejor iteración (CV):", best_iter_gbm, "\n")
## GBM mejor iteración (CV): 114
pred_gbm <- predict(modelo_gbm, newdata = data_test, n.trees = best_iter_gbm)
cat(sprintf("RMSE GBM en test: %.4f\n", Metrics::rmse(y_test, pred_gbm)))
## RMSE GBM en test: 2.9021

6.4.1 Curva de aprendizaje GBM

# Extraer errores del objeto gbm de forma segura
n_iter <- length(modelo_gbm$train.error)

if (n_iter > 0 && length(modelo_gbm$cv.error) == n_iter) {
  gbm_log <- data.frame(
    iter  = seq_len(n_iter),
    Train = modelo_gbm$train.error,
    CV    = modelo_gbm$cv.error
  ) %>%
    pivot_longer(cols = c(Train, CV),
                 names_to = "Conjunto", values_to = "Error")

  ggplot(gbm_log, aes(iter, Error, color = Conjunto)) +
    geom_line(linewidth = 0.7, alpha = 0.85) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = best_iter_gbm, linetype = "dashed",
               color = "black", linewidth = 0.8) +
    scale_color_manual(values = c("Train" = "steelblue", "CV" = "tomato")) +
    labs(title    = "Curva de aprendizaje — GBM",
         subtitle = paste("Mejor iteración (CV) =", best_iter_gbm),
         x = "Iteración", y = "Error cuadrático medio",
         color = "Conjunto") +
    theme_bw(base_size = 12) +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom")
} else {
  # Fallback: solo CV error (el más importante)
  gbm_log <- data.frame(
    iter  = seq_along(modelo_gbm$cv.error),
    Error = modelo_gbm$cv.error
  )
  ggplot(gbm_log, aes(iter, Error)) +
    geom_line(color = "tomato", linewidth = 0.7) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = best_iter_gbm, linetype = "dashed",
               color = "black", linewidth = 0.8) +
    labs(title    = "Curva de aprendizaje — GBM (solo CV)",
         subtitle = paste("Mejor iteración (CV) =", best_iter_gbm),
         x = "Iteración", y = "CV Error") +
    theme_bw(base_size = 12)
}

Curva de aprendizaje del GBM: error train vs. CV

7 XGBoost

7.1 Modelo base con early stopping

params_base <- list(
  objective = "reg:squarederror", eval_metric = "rmse",
  eta = 0.05, max_depth = 5, min_child_weight = 3,
  subsample = 0.8, colsample_bytree = 0.8, gamma = 0
)

set.seed(SEED)
cv_base <- xgb.cv(params = params_base, data = dtrain,
                  nrounds = 2000, nfold = 5,
                  early_stopping_rounds = 50,
                  print_every_n = 200, verbose = 1)
## Multiple eval metrics are present. Will use test_rmse for early stopping.
## Will train until test_rmse hasn't improved in 50 rounds.
## 
## [1]  train-rmse:2.881585±0.017297    test-rmse:2.897175±0.068529 
## Stopping. Best iteration:
## [63] train-rmse:2.187170±0.016185    test-rmse:2.918225±0.046521
## 
## [63] train-rmse:2.187170±0.016185    test-rmse:2.918225±0.046521
nrounds_base <- cv_base$best_iteration
if (is.null(nrounds_base) || is.na(nrounds_base) || nrounds_base < 1) {
  nrounds_base <- which.min(cv_base$evaluation_log$test_rmse_mean)
}
cat(sprintf("XGB base — nrounds óptimo: %d\n", nrounds_base))
## XGB base — nrounds óptimo: 13

7.1.1 Curva de aprendizaje XGBoost base

cv_base$evaluation_log %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(train_rmse_mean, test_rmse_mean),
    names_to = "Conjunto", values_to = "RMSE"
  ) %>%
  mutate(Conjunto = recode(Conjunto,
    train_rmse_mean = "Train",
    test_rmse_mean  = "CV Test")) %>%
  ggplot(aes(iter, RMSE, color = Conjunto)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.7) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = nrounds_base, linetype = "dashed",
             color = "black", linewidth = 0.8) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Train" = "steelblue", "CV Test" = "tomato")) +
  labs(title = "Curva de aprendizaje — XGBoost base",
       subtitle = paste("Mejor iteración =", nrounds_base),
       x = "Iteración", y = "RMSE", color = "Conjunto") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 12) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")

Curva de aprendizaje XGBoost base (CV 5 folds) 

set.seed(SEED)
modelo_xgb <- xgb.train(params = params_base, data = dtrain,
                         nrounds = nrounds_base,
                         watchlist = list(train = dtrain, test = dtest),
                         verbose = 0)
pred_xgb <- predict(modelo_xgb, dtest)
cat(sprintf("RMSE XGBoost base en test: %.4f\n", Metrics::rmse(y_test, pred_xgb)))
## RMSE XGBoost base en test: 2.9043

7.2 Diagnóstico: curvas CV-RMSE por learning rate

eta_range <- c(0.001, 0.01, 0.05, 0.1, 0.3)
df_eta <- map_dfr(eta_range, function(e) {
  set.seed(SEED)
  xgb.cv(data = dtrain,
         params = list(objective = "reg:squarederror",
                       eta = e, max_depth = 6, subsample = 0.8),
         nrounds = 1500, nfold = 5,
         metrics = "rmse", verbose = 0)$evaluation_log %>%
    select(iter, test_rmse_mean) %>%
    mutate(eta = factor(e))
})

ggplot(df_eta, aes(iter, test_rmse_mean, color = eta)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.7) +
  labs(title = "Curvas CV-RMSE según learning rate (stress_level)",
       subtitle = "Comparación de 5 valores de eta",
       x = "Iteración", y = "CV RMSE", color = "eta") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 12) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")

Curvas de CV-RMSE para distintos valores de eta (learning rate)

7.3 XGBoost tuneado con tidymodels (Latin Hypercube)

Se realiza una búsqueda de hiperparámetros con CV repetida (5 folds × 3 repeticiones) y una grilla Latin Hypercube de 40 combinaciones.

modelo_tm <- boost_tree(
  mode           = "regression",
  trees          = tune(),
  tree_depth     = tune(),
  learn_rate     = tune(),
  loss_reduction = tune(),
  min_n          = tune(),
  mtry           = tune(),
  sample_size    = tune()
) %>% set_engine("xgboost")

receta <- recipe(stress_level ~ ., data = data_train) %>%
  step_dummy(all_nominal_predictors(), one_hot = TRUE) %>%
  step_zv(all_predictors())

wf <- workflow() %>% add_recipe(receta) %>% add_model(modelo_tm)

params_tune <- extract_parameter_set_dials(wf) %>%
  finalize(data_train %>% select(-stress_level))

set.seed(SEED)
cv_folds <- vfold_cv(data_train, v = 5, repeats = 3, strata = stress_level)

lhs_grid <- if (exists("grid_space_filling", where = asNamespace("dials"))) {
  dials::grid_space_filling(params_tune, size = 40, type = "latin_hypercube")
} else {
  dials::grid_latin_hypercube(params_tune, size = 40)
}

n_cores   <- suppressWarnings(parallel::detectCores())
if (is.na(n_cores) || n_cores < 2) n_cores <- 2
n_workers <- max(1L, min(n_cores - 1L, 4L))

cl <- NULL
ok_paralelo <- tryCatch({
  cl <- makePSOCKcluster(n_workers)
  registerDoParallel(cl)
  TRUE
}, error = function(e) {
  message("Paralelización no disponible; sigo en serie.")
  FALSE
})

set.seed(SEED)
grid_fit <- tune_grid(
  object    = wf,
  resamples = cv_folds,
  metrics   = metric_set(yardstick::rmse, yardstick::mae, yardstick::rsq),
  grid      = lhs_grid,
  control   = control_grid(save_pred = TRUE, verbose = FALSE)
)

if (ok_paralelo && !is.null(cl)) { stopCluster(cl); registerDoSEQ() }

cat("\nTop 5 combinaciones (RMSE):\n")
## 
## Top 5 combinaciones (RMSE):
print(show_best(grid_fit, metric = "rmse", n = 5))
## # A tibble: 5 × 13
##    mtry trees min_n tree_depth learn_rate loss_reduction sample_size .metric
##   <int> <int> <int>      <int>      <dbl>          <dbl>       <dbl> <chr>  
## 1     7   248    11          5    0.00381       6.55e- 6       0.685 rmse   
## 2     8   190     9         10    0.00249       4.10e- 2       0.750 rmse   
## 3     9  1648     5          1    0.00922       7.46e- 1       0.649 rmse   
## 4     8   362    18         13    0.00198       1.52e-10       0.899 rmse   
## 5     4     8    13          3    0.0194        1.51e- 7       0.906 rmse   
## # ℹ 5 more variables: .estimator <chr>, mean <dbl>, n <int>, std_err <dbl>,
## #   .config <chr>
mejores_hp <- select_best(grid_fit, metric = "rmse")
cat("\nMejores hiperparámetros:\n")
## 
## Mejores hiperparámetros:
print(mejores_hp)

11 Nested CV: estimación insesgada del error

La evaluación en el test set único puede sesgar a la baja el error de generalización porque el ganador se elige implícitamente según ese test. La CV anidada separa estrictamente el tuning (folds internos) de la evaluación (folds externos), produciendo un estimador insesgado.

Coste computacional: 5 outer folds × (3 inner folds × 20 combinaciones) = 300 ajustes.

set.seed(SEED)
outer_folds <- vfold_cv(datos, v = 5, strata = stress_level)

fit_outer_fold <- function(split) {
  train_in <- analysis(split)
  test_in  <- assessment(split)

  inner_folds <- vfold_cv(train_in, v = 3, strata = stress_level)
  inner_params <- extract_parameter_set_dials(wf) %>%
    finalize(train_in %>% select(-stress_level))
  inner_grid <- if (exists("grid_space_filling", where = asNamespace("dials"))) {
    dials::grid_space_filling(inner_params, size = 20, type = "latin_hypercube")
  } else {
    dials::grid_latin_hypercube(inner_params, size = 20)
  }

  inner_fit <- tune_grid(
    object    = wf,
    resamples = inner_folds,
    metrics   = metric_set(yardstick::rmse),
    grid      = inner_grid,
    control   = control_grid(verbose = FALSE)
  )
  best_in <- select_best(inner_fit, metric = "rmse")
  fitted  <- finalize_workflow(wf, best_in) %>% fit(data = train_in)
  preds   <- predict(fitted, new_data = test_in)$.pred
  list(rmse = Metrics::rmse(test_in$stress_level, preds), hp = best_in)
}

cat("Lanzando nested CV...\n")
## Lanzando nested CV...
if (ok_paralelo) {
  cl2 <- tryCatch(makePSOCKcluster(n_workers), error = function(e) NULL)
  if (!is.null(cl2)) registerDoParallel(cl2)
}

nested_out <- lapply(outer_folds$splits, fit_outer_fold)

if (exists("cl2") && !is.null(cl2)) { stopCluster(cl2); registerDoSEQ() }

rmses_nested <- vapply(nested_out, `[[`, numeric(1), "rmse")

cat(sprintf(
  "\n>> Nested CV RMSE: %.3f ± %.3f  (min = %.3f, max = %.3f, n = %d folds)\n",
  mean(rmses_nested), sd(rmses_nested),
  min(rmses_nested), max(rmses_nested), length(rmses_nested)))
## 
## >> Nested CV RMSE: 2.899 ± 0.026  (min = 2.863, max = 2.923, n = 5 folds)

11.1 Gráfico de resultados Nested CV

data.frame(
  Fold = paste0("Fold ", seq_along(rmses_nested)),
  RMSE = rmses_nested
) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = Fold, y = RMSE, fill = Fold)) +
  geom_col(alpha = 0.8, show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = mean(rmses_nested), linetype = "dashed",
             color = "steelblue", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = Metrics::rmse(y_test, pred_tm),
             linetype = "dotdash", color = "tomato", linewidth = 1) +
  annotate("text", x = 0.6, y = mean(rmses_nested) + 0.005,
           label = sprintf("Media nested = %.3f", mean(rmses_nested)),
           hjust = 0, color = "steelblue", size = 3.5) +
  annotate("text", x = 0.6, y = Metrics::rmse(y_test, pred_tm) - 0.005,
           label = sprintf("Single split = %.3f", Metrics::rmse(y_test, pred_tm)),
           hjust = 0, color = "tomato", size = 3.5) +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Pastel1") +
  labs(title = "Nested CV — RMSE por fold externo",
       subtitle = "Azul = media nested | Rojo = RMSE test único (XGB tuned)",
       x = "Fold externo", y = "RMSE") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 12) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"))

11.3 Comparación single split vs. nested CV

rmse_single <- Metrics::rmse(y_test, pred_tm)
rmse_nested <- mean(rmses_nested)
sesgo       <- rmse_single - rmse_nested

cat(sprintf(
  "RMSE single test split (XGB tuned): %.4f\nRMSE nested CV (medio):              %.4f\nDiferencia (sesgo optimista est.):   %.4f\n",
  rmse_single, rmse_nested, sesgo))
## RMSE single test split (XGB tuned): 2.9065
## RMSE nested CV (medio):              2.8986
## Diferencia (sesgo optimista est.):   0.0079
# Tabla resumen
data.frame(
  Método   = c("Single split (XGB tuned)", "Nested CV (medio)"),
  RMSE     = round(c(rmse_single, rmse_nested), 4),
  Interpretación = c("Puede ser optimista", "Estimación insesgada")
) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = "Comparación de estimaciones del error de generalización")

12 Conclusiones

12.1 Resumen ejecutivo

  • Mejor modelo en test (menor RMSE): rpart con RMSE = 2.870 [IC95%: 2.702 – 3.046].
  • La Nested CV estima un RMSE medio de 2.899 ± 0.026, lo que sugiere un sesgo optimista de aproximadamente 0.008 al usar un único test split.
  • Los predictores más relevantes (consenso RF + XGBoost) se visualizan en la sección de importancias.
  • Los residuos del mejor modelo no presentan completamente una distribución normal centrada en cero (Shapiro p = 0.000; t-test p = 0.973).
